Well let me tell you!

All Warsaw Pact materiel got code names. NATO had a lot of members speaking different languages, so they standardized names to help reduce confusion.

These names had rules so even if you didn't recognize the exact name, you still knew the general type of equipment being referenced. Examples:

Piston driven aircraft = monosyllabic word

Jet aircraft = multisyllabic word

Fighters = F

Bombers = B

So, a "Bear" is a propeller driven bomber, but a "Blackjack" is a jet bomber.

Similarly, a "Flanker" is a jet fighter. They pretty much finished with propeller fighters before the names came up.

This applies to other types of materiel, too: A is air-to-air missile ("Atoll"), G is ground-to-air ("Guideline"), S is surface to surface ("Scud"). The list goes on!
